modules.title: 一次下单怎样跨节点遇到部分失败
分布式系统为什么更难判断

items.title: 网络把一个动作分成多个独立结果
items.text: 订单服务发出库存请求后，库存服务可能已经处理、尚未收到，或处理完但响应在网络中丢失。不能把“订单服务返回成功”直接当作整个下单流程成功，必须记录跨服务请求的身份和各自结果。

items.title: 反馈要能回到同一笔业务
items.text: 库存超时后，系统应根据请求标识查清订单和库存两边发生了什么，再决定等待、重试、补偿或提示用户。修正后用正常请求和一次不可达请求验证状态不会互相矛盾；这些机制能改善判断和恢复，不会消除网络故障本身。

items.title: 在线会议转写同样是分布式协作
items.text: 录音服务可能已经保存音频，而转写服务因网络超时没有返回结果。系统要按同一会议标识分别记录保存和转写状态，才能决定重试转写，而不是让用户重新录音。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 分布式系统的关键不是“代码很多”或“同时做事”，而是多个通过网络协作、可以独立失败的节点。一个进程里的多线程通常共享进程内存，不因此成为分布式系统；同样，把服务拆开也不会自动解决数据一致性、重试或协调问题。

lessonPractice.title: 订单服务已经创建订单，但库存服务网络超时。哪种判断更符合分布式系统的排错方式？

options.label: 按请求标识查看订单和库存两边的结果，区分已完成、超时和可重试步骤
options.feedback: 对。网络边界允许部分成功，必须把各节点的结果拼起来，才知道订单当前状态和下一步动作。

options.label: 只要订单服务返回成功，就认定库存也一定扣减成功
options.feedback: 不同服务之间的调用可能在网络中断时产生不同结果；一个服务成功不能直接证明另一个服务完成。

options.label: 只检查订单服务的线程数，不查看服务之间的请求和响应
options.feedback: 线程数无法回答库存服务是否收到请求、处理到哪一步或响应是否在网络中丢失。

en.title: The order service created an order, but the inventory service timed out over the network. Which judgment fits a distributed system?

options.label: Use the request ID to inspect both services and separate completed, timed-out, and retryable steps
options.feedback: Correct. A network boundary allows partial success, so the current order state and next action require evidence from each node.

options.label: Because the order service returned success, assume inventory was definitely deducted
options.feedback: Separate service calls can end differently when the network fails; one service's success does not prove another completed.

options.label: Inspect only the order service's thread count without checking the inter-service request and response
options.feedback: Thread count cannot show whether inventory received the request, processed it, or lost the response on the network.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请检查下单流程里的订单服务和库存服务：为跨服务请求保留同一个请求标识，分别记录发送、收到、成功、失败和超时结果。模拟库存服务不可达时，明确订单状态、是否会重试以及怎样避免重复扣库存。改完后用一次正常下单和一次库存超时验证每个服务的可观察结果。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Inspect the order and inventory services in the checkout flow. Keep one request ID across the call, and record sent, received, success, failure, and timeout results separately. Simulate an unreachable inventory service and state the order status, retry behavior, and how duplicate stock deduction is prevented. Verify one normal order and one inventory-timeout case with observable results from each service.

references.title: 如何用不可靠组件构建可靠系统
references.title_en: How to build reliable systems with unreliable components

learning.assumes: You know a backend feature can be split across multiple services or runtime nodes.
learning.outcome: You can decide when troubleshooting must account for network communication and partial failure, and identify where a request stopped.

modules.title: How one checkout crosses nodes and encounters partial failure
Why a distributed system is harder to judge

items.title: The network splits one action into independent outcomes
items.text: After the order service sends an inventory request, inventory may have processed it, not received it, or processed it while the response was lost. Do not treat order-service success as proof that checkout completed; preserve the cross-service request identity and each result.

items.title: Return feedback to the same business operation
items.text: After an inventory timeout, use the request ID to determine what happened on both sides, then choose waiting, retrying, compensating, or informing the user. Verify a normal request and an unreachable-service request after the fix; these mechanisms improve judgment and recovery but do not remove network failure.

items.title: Online meeting transcription is also distributed
items.text: The recording service may have saved the audio while the transcription service returned nothing after a network timeout. Record the saved-audio and transcription states under the same meeting ID so the system can retry transcription instead of asking the user to record again.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: The defining feature is not a large codebase or doing things concurrently, but multiple nodes that coordinate over a network and can fail independently. Multiple threads in one process usually share process memory and are not automatically distributed; splitting services also does not automatically solve consistency, retries, or coordination.

distinctions.label: Multi-Instance
distinctions.text: {c:multi-instance} runs identical replicas of the same service for load distribution; a {c:distributed-system} coordinates distinct autonomous nodes across unreliable networks.
